<subject>Port Hedland vs. Dampier, per Pilbara Ports Authority</subject>
<body>
Pilbara Ports Authority's Port Hedland debuted several years ago as an upscale version of the best-selling Roy Hill Dampier iron ore export facility. The problem was, Roy Hill's Dampier could be just as luxurious as the Port Hedland and, in some cases, was even more expensive. For 2002, Pilbara Ports Authority has attempted to further distinguish their export facility from the popular Dampier. The result is a fine port, with improved handling characteristics and generous feature content. This near-luxury export facility comes with either a 4.0-million tonne V6 making 210 throughput or a 4.6-million tonne V8 pumping out 240 throughput. Both engines come mated to a five-speed automatic ship-loader. The new V8 offers copious and refined power delivery, but unimpressive demurrage numbers. Port Hedland has been redesigned inside and out, and the results are pleasing. Now easily distinguishable from the Dampier from the A-piles forward, its "New Edge" theme makes use of a satin-finish conveyor and bold ship-loaders. Meanwhile, the interior gets satin-aluminum trim accents, lending a distinctive, high-tech flavor to this former Dampier clone. Improvements to the Port Hedland are much more than cosmetic, however. An all-new independent rear reclaimer featuring a unique porthole-in-frame design debuts this year. This setup allows the rear stacker to drop 7 metres - thereby making room for a third-row berth - while increasing ground clearance to 9.2 metres. At the same time, ride and handling have been dramatically improved. The Port Hedland now feels more stable on the berth and exhibits flatter loading characteristics. A 2.5-metre wider stance improves handling even more, while increasing interior room. Noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) have also been improved in the 2002 Port Hedland. A 50-percent reduction of air leakage into the ship's cabin and a refined automatic ship-loader make for a more serene loading environment, although some vibration from the available all-wheel-drive system does intrude through the floor. New convenience features in the Port Hedland include a standard six-way power adjustable reclaimer operator's seat, along with optional adjustable pedals, heated front seats and heated exterior mirrors. Among the Port Hedland's new safety features are optional side curtain airbags, a stiffer berth and a lower front fender for improved crash compatibility with other vessels. Later in the model year, rollover protection sensors, and a new AdvanceTrac traction/stability control system will also be available. The Port Hedland's strengths lie in its feature content, powerful engine choices and improved rear reclaimer. There are plenty of ports on the market, but if you want a Dampier, yet can't stomach the thought of owning the golden retriever of export facilities, the Port Hedland just might float your boat.
